scope: Both adb mode-guidance and session-lifecycle FRs; sudohand migration stays parked.

audit.naming: Core exports, module filenames and CLI names match; reconnect/restart join the existing browser lifecycle family.
audit.parameters: Core signatures/docstrings drive actual --help and generated wrappers. Existing start/connect arguments remain compatible; page calls take the same connection-scoped --session-id.
audit.discovery: Start/connect first lines distinguish isolated launch from attaching real Chrome. One shared core guidance covers headless task selection, explicit/env/default precedence, GUI prerequisites, real device identity, same-page collaboration and remote adapter versus host viewer/relay responsibilities.
audit.returns: Legacy result fields remain. Observed session/profile identity, actual headless mode where known, ownership and capabilities are additive. Opaque automation_target_id is distinct from zero-based targets.index. External physical process fields remain null when unknown.
audit.failures: Stable unsupported=6, conflict/session_changed=5, target_closed/not_found=4, auth_failed=7, transient=9. Hints come from core Failure sections. No implicit transport/profile fallback or input replay.
audit.sync_async: Async connect/reconnect use wrap_core; sync start/disconnect/stop/restart use wrap_core_sync. An async SDK caller with a held CDP connection awaits browser.close on its own loop.
audit.generation: 63 generated tools; generator reports zero changes after regeneration. Integration scenarios are generated with integration-test-generator, then linted/formatted.
audit.composition: Reuses Chrome spawn, BrowserClient, page navigation/input and bridge. Two additional lifecycle primitives manage process/identity state that in-page JS cannot express.
audit.paid_model_limits: Four final workflows passed using real credentials and Chrome, names/first lines and actual help in isolated model context. This is observed workflow success, not a promise of perfect choices across all model runs.

capability_bounds.already_running_extension: Connect preserves Chrome/profile/unrelated tabs. It identifies actual extension profile and browser-run UUID; no attempt to infer unknown OS PID/path or change running headless mode.
capability_bounds.external_restart: Explicit authorization is required; unknown executable/start settings still return unsupported.
capability_bounds.extension_launch: Requires a persistently installed/enabled bridge in the specified existing profile. No remote-debugging or command-line extension loading flags. Busy profile conflicts without killing it.
capability_bounds.slow_handshake: Keeps the launched browser running, reports resources and persists its observed process identity. A later handshake on the nonce URL restores ownership.
capability_bounds.remote: Page images/input and remote page/X11 adapters are shipped after integrating PR #14. remote_adapters names bundled adapters; it does not assert a configured viewer, system X11 dependencies or a relay. Hosts retain viewer authentication, target/control ownership and cloud pairing.
